A group of students was given the task of planning a method to find the effects of the
For
growth regulator gibberellin (GA) on the germination of maize grains.
Examiner’s
Use
The students looked up information about investigations into the germination of maize.
The information that the students found is listed below.
• Maize needs to be soaked in water for 24 hours to stimulate germination.
• Maize starts to germinate 48–72 hours after soaking.
• GA promotes germination by activating a gene that causes the synthesis of the
enzyme amylase.
• The range of concentrations at which GA is found in plants is between
−3
1–10μmol dm .
• Amylase is released by the aleurone layer into the endosperm of the maize grain to
hydrolyse the starch reserves.
• The activity of amylase can be estimated by cutting the maize grains lengthways
into two halves and placing the cut sides onto agar containing starch in Petri dishes.
• After incubation at a constant temperature, iodine solution is used to test the agar
for the presence of starch.
The students carried out a preliminary investigation using maize grains that had been soaked
−3
in a 3 mmol dm solution of GA.
Fig. 1.1 shows the arrangement of cut maize grains that the students decided to use for their
main investigation and the results of testing the agar for starch using iodine solution after
incubation.
